system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Miami, United States. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Miami itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Miami space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Little Haiti/Little River, Allapattah, Wynwood, Design District, Downtown, Coral Gables, Miami Beach, Doral) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Miami spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Miami, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Fredric Snitzer Gallery
galleries.note: Miami's foundational contemporary dealer since the 1970s; launched Hernan Bas, Bert Rodriguez and the New World School generation, and an anchor exhibitor at Art Basel Miami Beach.

galleries.name: David Castillo Gallery
galleries.note: Nationally respected programme centered on Black and Latinx artists (Xaviera Simmons, Sanford Biggers, Pepe Mar); regular at Art Basel, Frieze and Armory with strong museum placements.

galleries.name: Nina Johnson
galleries.note: Formerly Gallery Diet; a critically watched programme blending art, craft and design (Katie Stout, Emmett Moore, Jim Drain) in a landmark Little Haiti compound.

galleries.name: Locust Projects
galleries.note: Miami's most influential nonprofit since 1998, commissioning ambitious site-specific installations and incubating artists later shown by major museums.

galleries.name: Emerson Dorsch
galleries.note: Operating since 1991, a pillar of the local scene with a research-driven roster of Florida-rooted conceptual and material practices.

galleries.name: Spinello Projects
galleries.note: Anthony Spinello's risk-taking programme launched Typoe, Agustina Woodgate and Antonia Wright; a key link between Miami's alternative and commercial worlds.

galleries.name: Mindy Solomon Gallery
galleries.note: Ceramics-forward contemporary programme with a strong national fair presence and consistent museum acquisitions.

galleries.name: Central Fine
galleries.note: Ibett Yanez's tightly curated Miami Beach space, known for sharp conceptual and minimalist exhibitions and collaborations with international artists.

galleries.name: Piero Atchugarry Gallery
galleries.note: Uruguayan gallery whose large Little Haiti space brings Latin American and European artists to Miami with a serious international fair schedule.

galleries.name: Oolite Arts
galleries.note: Formerly ArtCenter/South Florida; the region's largest artist-support organization, with studios, grants and free public exhibitions (new Little River campus in development).

galleries.name: Bakehouse Art Complex
galleries.note: Since 1985 the city's largest artist studio complex and exhibition hall, a training ground for generations of Miami artists.

galleries.name: El Espacio 23
galleries.note: Jorge M. Pérez's free public exhibition space and residency, staging curated shows of global contemporary art that draw international critical attention.

galleries.name: The Margulies Collection at the Warehouse
galleries.note: Martin Margulies's 45,000-sq-ft nonprofit exhibition space; monumental installations and photography that set a benchmark for Miami's collector-led spaces.

galleries.name: Primary
galleries.note: Grew out of the artist-run Primary Projects; irreverent, design-savvy exhibitions and public projects that shaped Miami's post-graffiti generation.

galleries.name: Dimensions Variable
galleries.note: Artist-run nonprofit with a rigorous, conceptually driven exhibition and residency programme respected far beyond Florida.

galleries.name: Pan American Art Projects
galleries.note: Long-running specialist in Cuban and Latin American modern and contemporary art, with a scholarly exhibition and publishing record.

galleries.name: Gary Nader Art Centre
galleries.note: Vast Latin American modern and contemporary showroom and sculpture park; a market power center for Botero, Lam and Matta in the Americas.

galleries.name: LnS Gallery
galleries.note: Sergio Cernuda and Luisa Lignarolo's polished programme of Cuban-American and Miami-based contemporary artists, with strong institutional ties.

galleries.name: Voloshyn Gallery
galleries.note: Kyiv gallery with a permanent Miami outpost; internationally covered for sustaining Ukrainian contemporary art through the war.

galleries.name: Fountainhead Arts
galleries.note: Residency and studio complex that has hosted well over a thousand artists, connecting visiting practitioners with Miami collectors and curators.

galleries.name: Superblue Miami
galleries.note: Experiential art destination founded with Pace, presenting large-scale immersive commissions by teamLab, Es Devlin and James Turrell.

galleries.name: Faena Art
galleries.note: Commissions ambitious performance and installation projects in the Rem Koolhaas–designed Faena Forum, a fixture of Art Week programming.

galleries.name: YoungArts
galleries.note: National artist-development foundation whose Miami campus gallery and Jewel Box present exhibitions, performances and alumni projects free to the public.

galleries.name: Cernuda Arte
galleries.note: The leading authority on Cuban art from the colonial era to the present; catalogues and scholarship used by museums worldwide.

galleries.name: N'Namdi Contemporary
galleries.note: Miami branch of the historic N'Namdi family galleries, a leading platform for African American abstraction and diaspora artists.

galleries.name: Dot Fiftyone Gallery
galleries.note: Two-decade Miami presence showing emerging and mid-career Latin American and local artists; a Wynwood pioneer that moved north with the scene.

galleries.name: Diaspora Vibe Cultural Arts Incubator
galleries.note: Since 1996 the key incubator for Caribbean and Latin American diaspora artists in Miami, with residencies, mentorship and exhibitions.

galleries.name: Little Haiti Cultural Complex
galleries.note: City-run cultural center whose galleries are the primary public venue for Haitian and Haitian-American contemporary art in Miami.

galleries.name: Ascaso Gallery
galleries.note: Venezuelan-founded gallery known for kinetic and geometric abstraction alongside contemporary Latin American painters.

galleries.name: KDR Miami
galleries.note: Younger dealer (KDR305) with a sharp emerging-artist programme and an active satellite-fair presence during Miami Art Week.

galleries.name: Jupiter Contemporary
galleries.note: North Beach gallery showing emerging international painters and sculptors; a critically noted newcomer to the Miami dealer landscape.

galleries.name: Green Space Miami
galleries.note: Free nonprofit gallery pairing social-issue exhibitions with community programming; a rising fixture on the Biscayne corridor.

galleries.name: Laundromat Art Space
galleries.note: Artist-run studios and gallery in a former laundromat; a low-cost launchpad for emerging Miami artists and curators.

galleries.name: Bridge Red Studios
galleries.note: Artist-run North Miami space known for thoughtful, curator-driven group shows and support of veteran local artists.

galleries.name: Under the Bridge
galleries.note: Independent exhibition space in the same warehouse complex, giving experimental and mid-career artists room for unconventional projects.

galleries.name: Swampspace
galleries.note: Oliver Sanchez's long-running guerrilla-spirited storefront, a Design District holdout for unfiltered artist-run programming.

galleries.name: Cannonball
galleries.note: Formerly LegalArt; residencies, fellowships and the Fringe Projects public art commissions that put artists into the civic realm.

galleries.name: Edge Zones
galleries.note: Charo Oquet's long-running artist-run center for performance, experimental and Caribbean diaspora practices.

galleries.name: Durban Segnini Gallery
galleries.note: Four decades of Latin American geometric abstraction and constructivism, with a deep secondary-market inventory.

galleries.name: Ideobox Artspace
galleries.note: Wynwood mainstay presenting Latin American contemporary artists with a consistent, curatorially framed programme.

galleries.name: Robert Fontaine Gallery
galleries.note: Established Wynwood dealer bridging pop, street-derived and blue-chip editions for Miami collectors.

galleries.name: Opera Gallery Miami
galleries.note: Miami branch of the international chain; high-traffic Design District showroom for modern masters and market-driven contemporary names.

galleries.name: Markowicz Fine Art
galleries.note: Design District dealer in contemporary photography, pop and sculpture, with a visible role in the district's art retail scene.

galleries.name: Avant Gallery
galleries.note: Brickell gallery introducing emerging contemporary painters and sculptors to Miami's condo-collector market.

galleries.name: Lelia Mordoch Gallery
galleries.note: Paris gallery with a permanent Wynwood space, specializing in kinetic, optical and light-based art.

galleries.name: Kavachnina Contemporary
galleries.note: Longstanding Wynwood gallery showing Russian, European and Latin American contemporary artists in a large warehouse space.

galleries.name: Now Contemporary Art
galleries.note: Wynwood gallery focused on emerging Latin American and Caribbean artists, with regular satellite-fair participation.

galleries.name: Harold Golen Gallery
galleries.note: Miami's dedicated home for lowbrow, pop-surrealist and outsider-adjacent art; a Wynwood original.

galleries.name: Kendall Art Center
galleries.note: Home of the Rodríguez Collection of Cuban art, with rotating exhibitions and programming for South Miami-Dade.

galleries.name: Aluna Art Foundation
galleries.note: Curator-run nonprofit (Adriana Herrera and Willy Castellanos) producing scholarly exhibitions on Latin American conceptual practices.

galleries.name: Turn-Based Press
galleries.note: Printmaking studio and gallery collaborating with local and visiting artists on editions and exhibitions.

galleries.name: The Center for Subtropical Affairs
galleries.note: Artist-run compound blending ecology, food and exhibitions; a distinctive node in Miami's alternative-space network.

galleries.name: Sammer Gallery
galleries.note: Veteran dealer in Latin American modernism and geometric abstraction, long active with Miami institutions and fairs.

galleries.name: Rudolf Budja Gallery
galleries.note: Austrian dealer's Miami Beach space handling Warhol, postwar editions and contemporary secondary-market work.

galleries.name: Zu Galeria Fine Arts
galleries.note: Calle Ocho gallery central to Little Havana's Viernes Culturales, showing Cuban and Cuban-American artists.

galleries.name: Curator's Voice Art Projects
galleries.note: Milagros Bello's curatorially framed Wynwood space, consistently thematic exhibitions of emerging Latin American artists.

galleries.name: Gregg Shienbaum Fine Art
galleries.note: Wynwood dealer in pop, street and postwar editions, a steady presence on the district's gallery walk.

galleries.name: Kelley Roy Gallery
galleries.note: Wynwood gallery and event space showing contemporary painting and sculpture by Florida-based and international artists.

galleries.name: Wynwood Walls
galleries.note: Tony Goldman's outdoor mural park with an indoor gallery; the single most visible driver of Wynwood's transformation into an arts district.

galleries.name: Etra Fine Art
galleries.note: Miami dealer in postwar and contemporary works on paper and editions, active with local collectors and Art Week programming.
